steps.title: Squeak or growl?
steps.text: A mouse squeaks. A bear growls. Why do they sound so different?

steps.prompt: Is this a mouse sound or a bear sound?
steps.reveal: A mouse! That was a high sound.
A bear! That was a low sound.

steps.intro: Stand up! When the sound is high, stretch up tall. When it's low, crouch down small. {engineer}, you press the buttons.

steps.title: Fast wiggles sound high
steps.text: High sounds are fast wiggles. Low sounds are slow wiggles. Look how squashed up the high wiggles are!

wow.text: The note A wiggles the air 440 times every second. Much too fast to count!

steps.intro: Slide your finger up the ladder: the sound goes up! Slide down, and it goes down.
Listen to two notes. Did the sound go up, or down?
When our robot grabs a star, the game needs a star sound: two quick notes. You choose them!
Grab the stars and listen for your star sound!

steps.title: A rubber-band guitar
need: A tissue box or a shoebox
Four rubber bands, thick and thin
steps: A grown-up stretches the bands round the open box.
Pluck each band, gently then harder.
Pull one band tighter and pluck it again. Does it sound higher?
steps.why: Thin or tight bands wiggle fast and sound high. Thick or loose bands wiggle slowly and sound low.
steps.safety: Bands can snap: a grown-up fits them and keeps them away from faces.

debrief: Can you sing the highest note you can? And the lowest?
